note: Report points for the test TGS (Swanston St southbound closed, Faraday St to Grattan St), written in advance so the demo makes no Claude call. Used with the saved TGS analysis and the demo site scan. Every number comes from a source listed in `made_from`.
made_from: SUMO result for this closure: model/sumo/output/smac/facts.json and data/impact/sumo-smac.json

Test TGS drawing positions: data/test/make-smac-tgs.mjs (lane closure 2 to 86 m, work area 22 to 60 m north of Grattan St, TC 1 at 89 m, VMS 2 at 130 m, VMS 1 at 182 m, all on the east side). Faraday St is about 206 m north of Grattan St.

OpenStreetMap (model/sumo/work/smac/area.osm): Melbourne University tram stop platform 100 to 158 m north of Grattan St; signalised crossing at its south end, 91 m; zebra crossings with no signals on every leg of Faraday St and Cardigan St; bus 546 terminus bays and bus 402 stops on Grattan St

City of Melbourne pedestrian counts, typical weekday over 8 weeks to 30 Sep 2026: Grattan St-Swanston St (West) sensor, 38 m from the scan, busiest works hour 1pm to 2pm at 708 people an hour (690 from 12pm to 1pm)
Demo site scan, measured by lib/scan/measure.ts: 34.9 m of street, kerb 170 mm, footpath width not measurable, tram tracks not reached
sources: Tram stops, crossings and bus routes from OpenStreetMap

actions.title: Move VMS 1 and 2 before Faraday St
actions.summary: Both boards stand past the only turn onto the detour.
actions.impact: About 150 drivers an hour read "Detour via Faraday St" too late, reach the closure and turn around beside the tram stop.
actions.why: Drivers turning around in a closed lane next to tram tracks and a busy crossing put walkers, riders and the traffic controllers at risk.
actions.recommendation: Place VMS 1 on Swanston St north of Faraday St, before the turn, and VMS 2 further north, so drivers see both before they must turn.

actions.title: Measure the footpath before setup
actions.summary: The scan could not measure it, and 1.5 m is exactly what the lunchtime crowd needs.
actions.impact: A bin, sign or barrier foot that narrows the path below 1.5 m would push people onto the bike lane at lunchtime.
actions.why: About 708 people an hour walk past from 1pm to 2pm. Below 1.5 m clear the footpath gets crowded by the council's rule.
actions.recommendation: Tape-measure the narrowest point past the works before setup. Move bins or signs, or the barrier line, to keep at least 1.5 m clear.

actions.title: Guard the plant crossing
actions.summary: The only gap in the barriers opens onto a busy footpath and bike lane.
actions.impact: A reversing or turning machine meets walkers and riders who don't expect it.
actions.why: The plan relies on TC 1 and TC 2 to hold people, and the crowd is largest from noon to 2pm.
actions.recommendation: Have TC 1 and TC 2 stop walkers and riders for every plant crossing, and schedule deliveries and plant moves outside noon to 2pm.

actions.title: Apply for the PTV permit
actions.summary: The closure and VMS 2 are within 20 m of the tram stop.
actions.impact: Without the permit the works can be stopped on the day.
actions.why: Works within 20 m of a tram stop need a PTV permit, and works near the tracks need Yarra Trams approval.
actions.recommendation: Send the plan to PTV and Yarra Trams together, with the barrier clearance to the tram envelope marked.
